paper.title_en: Amortized conditional inference under changing parameter information in small-angle X-ray scattering
paper.abstract_en: Many scientific measurements do not uniquely determine the physical system that produced them. Different parameter configurations may explain the same observations, and additional measurements or physical assumptions can change which explanations remain plausible. We develop an amortized conditional inference method to examine these alternatives as the available information changes. Using masked flow matching, the method approximates joint conditional posteriors when different parameters are supplied exactly or with uncertainty. This allows repeated analysis of the same measurement without retraining, while reusing its encoded representation. We can also examine the consequences of assumed parameter distributions and separately assess whether supplied information is compatible with the observation-only posterior. We validate the learned conditionals against analytic posteriors and compare posterior accuracy and inference cost in a simulated scattering benchmark, where the compressed architecture performs better than joint attention on both measures. We apply the method to small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) of cellulose fibrils in paper, examining structural ambiguities in simulated measurements and the effects of physical assumptions on experimental measurements of a paper during hydration. At high humidity, the inferred effective fibril size distribution broadens. Assuming that this distribution remains unchanged instead shifts the posterior towards increased interfibrillar separation, although both interpretations reproduce the measured curves similarly. The compatibility analysis identifies conserved parameter values that are difficult to reconcile with the wettest measurements.
